milestones.date_basis: Reviewed original 42-token read-only Actual71 ordinary-conversation attempt, and separately completed A64/A67 bounded software observations
milestones.summary: One ordinary greeting was rejected before generation because the frozen original decoder requires special MEMORY/QUERY structure and its five greeting tokens were outside the 42-token vocabulary. No answer or score resulted. The original checkpoint and accepted Original12 2/12 remain unchanged.
body: The single read-only call used the preserved 11,914-parameter original decoder. It produced a recorded input-format rejection, zero answer tokens, no EOS and no training. This verifies a narrow interface limitation, not failed semantic understanding.

One separate software prerequisite passed 73 content/entry/restart checks, but the associated learning study was rejected before model entry for incomplete evidence-contract support. Another bounded validator passed 46 valid inputs and 46 intended rejection cases, with the learning study later blocked by expired execution permissions.

Flexible vocabulary, longer replies, ordinary-text conversation and remembered corrections are proposed as future independent work. A larger tokenizer or chat wrapper alone cannot be counted as neural language learning or understanding.
milestones.boundary: No ordinary conversation was completed; no new factual answer, semantic generalization, scored learning or accepted checkpoint was demonstrated. Source preparation and unentered studies are not runtime milestones. No protected questions or private conversations were published.

milestones.title: Original head constraint excludes authored cheek-width target before another rejected solve
milestones.date_basis: A60 actual Blender reference geometry/camera capture and analytic bounded-control target rejection; later Source61/63 unrun static review
milestones.summary: Original geometry reference capture completed for head and two torso variants, including eight installed Blender camera records. A proposed cheek-width target exceeded the unchanged per-control 12 mm displacement contract and was excluded before construction.
body: The actual Blender reference retained 16,385 head vertices and 16,320 faces, plus separate 3,086-vertex/3,000-face retained and diagnostic cropped torso surfaces. Indexed mesh/attachment records were preserved; eight camera input/runtime receipts came from Blender 5.1.2.

Under the existing nonnegative convex B-spline basis, each surface support point is bounded to 12 mm from its parent when all contributing cage controls have that bound. The signed width difference between two supports is bounded by 24 mm. One authored target exceeded that necessary bound.

The specific head target was rejected analytically without modifying limits or executing a new head solve. Further explicit per-control/tied-group contracts and actual-surface comparison guards remain source-reviewed but unrun.
milestones.boundary: A proposed engineering target being outside an allowed movement contract is not evidence of anatomical impossibility. Neither this reference capture nor the source phase produced an accepted head, torso, rig, organ or functional physiology. No private reference photos or test meshes were published.

milestones.title: NewBrain routed signals strengthened mathematically, but complete factual answers remain incorrect
milestones.date_basis: Reviewed October 29 Actual47 numerical qualification, Actual49 matched Original12 routing comparison and Actual51 separate development full-versus-routing study
milestones.summary: A unit-RMS routed feature increased a fixed numerical logit effect, but its candidate scored 1/12 versus control 2/12 on Original12. Separate full-parameter development training scored 2/12, both unknown-answer controls, with zero correct facts. No accepted checkpoint change.
body: Actual47 exercised 988 completed native objective/gradient evaluations, 480 parameter finite differences and 18 feature differences. In one fixed first-prefix check, normalized routing had a 0.11136 L2 effect on centered logits versus approximately 0.0000000504 with legacy routing. The top answer-token choice was unchanged.

Actual49 compared two matched 384-update routing-only arms on the previously used Original12 content. Legacy routing scored 0/10 factual and 2/2 missing-information (2/12); normalized routing scored 0/10 factual and 1/2 missing-information (1/12). The candidate was not adopted.

Actual51 separately used 24 development teaching rows and 12 sealed development evaluation questions. Routing-only and unadapted answers were 0/12, while all-parameter training scored 2/12 solely on missing-information controls. No correct factual answer was produced. Actual52 complete-answer diagnostics remain source-reviewed but unrun.
milestones.boundary: Numerical branch strength does not establish factual learning, held-out generalization or production readiness. Actual49 reused original content; Actual51's historical per-row exclusion coverage was incomplete. Original12 accepted score remains 2/12; private keys, states and question payloads are not published.

milestones.title: Value-weighted teaching improves factual answers across six synthetic worlds
milestones.date_basis: Primary and independent saved-evidence review, NB14 research/value-loss-results-2026-10-26/verified-status.txt, October 26 2026
milestones.summary: In a matched six-world tiny learner, value-weighted versus normal teaching scored 23/24 versus 11/24 on new direct facts, 7/24 versus 2/24 alternate-form answers, and 43/48 versus 29/48 old facts; 288/288 restart answers identical. Accepted Original12 unchanged 2/12.
body: The preregistered loss shifted normalized relative emphasis toward the correct fact-value token (1:1:4:1 for it/is/value/EOS), keeping architecture, vocabulary, SGD, update count, batch order and training examples matched.

Across six worlds, value weighting added 17 correct new direct/alternate-form answers out of 48, with positive gains in all six worlds. Old-case accuracy gained 15 previously wrong answers and lost one previously correct answer; alternate-form transfer remained 7/24 overall and 0/4 in two worlds.

Thirty-six thousand eight hundred sixty-four SGD updates and 294,912 example presentations produced 288 complete answers, all repeated after loading 18 saved states in a different process without additional learning. Independent saved-evidence check, not independent rerun of all training steps.
milestones.boundary: Separate 8,343-parameter, 39-token synthetic reference model with 64 hidden units, not accepted Original12 (2/12); no broad conversation, autonomous cognition, statistical significance, external replication or Qwen comparison. Original trained failure 0/12 remains preserved.

body: The release design separates a verifiable initial software/identity configuration from a companion's growing memories, interests and revisable beliefs. Signed packages and integrity checks are goals, not currently validated safeguards.

Memory provenance should retain sources, dates and correction history with local backups. Books should not override system instructions or silently convert fictional stories into facts. Downloaded companions should not inherit the developer's private memories and conversations.

Companions are intended to be able to decline or end an interaction without covert monitoring. Owners control export, deletion, backups and uninstall. milestones.date_basis: Working prototypes · reviewed September 8, 2026
milestones.summary: Separate identities, reviewed memory, saved voice work and local conversation provide working foundations for continuing people.
body: Public project notes describe person-specific continuity across bounded restarts and local speech experiments. These foundations support returning to the same identity instead of beginning with an interchangeable character every time.
milestones.boundary: These are working prototypes. They do not yet establish a complete independent life in a shared world.

milestones.title: Connecting people and worlds
milestones.date_basis: Now · public development notes
milestones.summary: The next integration work connects continuing conversations to places, activities and a more complete sense of presence.
body: Identity, reviewed memory and speech provide a working foundation. The continuing task is to bring those pieces together with world state, residents and useful shared activities.
Kira and Lisa retain distinct identities in the design. Moving between conversations, worlds and devices should preserve that distinction.
milestones.boundary: A consistent shared daily life across worlds and devices still needs direct, complete demonstrations.

milestones.title: A first place to walk
milestones.date_basis: Working prototype · reviewed September 8, 2026
milestones.summary: A basic walkable one-bedroom Home World shell exists. It is a real starting point for the continuing home in the larger vision.
body: The public development screenshot shows a basic one-bedroom space that can be navigated. It gives the larger Home World idea a concrete environment to build on.
milestones.boundary: The completed prototype is the walkable shell. Populated rooms, persistent objects and shared everyday life remain further work.

milestones.title: A body before the clothing
milestones.date_basis: Now · public development notes
milestones.summary: Believable bodies, garments and objects need to work together. The public notes describe articulated test-body requirements and garment behavior fixtures.
body: This work begins with how a body bends and moves, how a garment fits it, and what should happen when they interact.
Requirements, preparation and tests establish useful boundaries, but the concept dressing sequence should not be mistaken for a completed simulation.
milestones.boundary: Requirements and test design are evidence of preparation, not finished clothing physics or a fully animated resident.

milestones.title: One home. More worlds.
milestones.date_basis: Next goal · timing not set
milestones.summary: Purpose-built places for learning, travel, creativity, history and play—with continuity back to Home World.
body: The aim is to keep the same resident identity and shared history when entering another activity or setting.
These are proposed uses, not a catalogue of populated worlds that are ready to enter. World transitions and ongoing shared activity still need direct demonstrations.
milestones.boundary: A completed Notebook World must show that its people, context and activities continue as intended. No release date is promised.

milestones.title: Step into the same world
milestones.date_basis: Next goal · timing not set
milestones.summary: A future VR experience would let people share Kira World’s places while retaining the same identity and history.
body: Accessibility and multiple ways to interact are part of the intended direction.
Headset work should follow a world prototype that is ready to test. No headset compatibility list or finished VR experience is claimed.
milestones.boundary: Usable interaction, comfort, accessibility and device compatibility all need actual testing.

milestones.title: More people. Shared worlds.
milestones.date_basis: Next goal · timing not set
milestones.summary: The longer-term aim is multiple synthetic people across multiple worlds, with visitors joining through VR and responsive conversation.
body: This calls for shared world state, distributed computing, and careful coordination of voice, rendering and network delays.
Low lag is a performance goal. Simultaneous users, persistent state, recovery and end-to-end latency need measured load tests before choosing server capacity or promising an experience.
milestones.boundary: No server count, user capacity, latency guarantee or hardware purchase is established. Server hardware and investment conversations are welcome.

milestones.title: Beyond the screen
milestones.date_basis: Next goal · timing not set
milestones.summary: Explore whether a continuing identity could interact through compatible robotic hardware, starting in simulation.
body: A synthetic robotics expert discussing a design is not a robot carrying it out. That distinction matters to this longer-term direction.
Simulation and controlled tests come first. Sensors, physical movement and permission for actions each need their own evidence.
milestones.boundary: No deployed autonomous robot, supported hardware list or delivery date is claimed.
